owner.occupation: Recreation coordinator at a long-term care home

world.bio: I am the recreation coordinator at a long-term care home in East York, Toronto. I plan the weekly programs for about ninety residents: bingo, chair yoga, gardening club, music afternoons. I keep a binder with every resident's favourite song and the year they first heard it. Outside work I volunteer at an animal shelter on Saturdays.
skills_assets: Recreation Therapy diploma from Humber College, 7 years in long-term care
A binder (and a spreadsheet) listing every resident's favourite song, year, and who they danced to it with
Experience running sing-alongs and reminiscence sessions for residents with dementia
A small budget of about $400 a month for activity supplies
Access to a volunteer list of about thirty people, including a few musicians
A Bluetooth speaker and a donated Casio keyboard that I carry between floors
A list of local community choirs and music students I've called over the years

projects.name: Fall Sing-Along Series
projects.text: A weekly Thursday afternoon sing-along in the main lounge, meant especially for residents with dementia. People who haven't spoken in days will sometimes mouth the words to old songs. The problem is the piano: the home's upright has been out of tune for two years, a few keys are dead, and the volunteer pianist, Mr. Alvarez, politely refuses to play it. For now I use a Casio keyboard and a playlist, but it is not the same. Residents look toward the piano, not the speaker.

projects.name: Memory Wall
projects.text: A wall in the second-floor hallway for photos and objects that families bring in. I have six families on board so far. Needs a budget I do not have, but I am looking at second-hand frames. Hoping to have it up before the holidays.

notes.text: Mrs. Petrova sang the whole first verse of 'Kalinka' today. Her daughter says she has not said a full sentence in months. I wrote it down on the binder page right away so I don't forget the date. These are the days that make the job feel real.

The second-floor residents had a fight over the remote control again. Mr. Peters and Mrs. Doyle, seventy years apart in personality, not in age. I made them co-hosts of the Wednesday movie. They have not spoken to each other since but at least they watch the same thing.

Tried to talk to admin about the piano again. They said the repair estimate was $2,800 and it is not in this year's budget. I asked about a second-hand upright instead. Was told to 'look into it' which usually means no.

Sister texted about the wedding in Montreal. Bridesmaid dress fitting is in two weeks and I still have not bought the shoes. Also I realized I need to book the train. Saving for the condo means saying no to a lot of things, including a new dress.
Volunteer day at the shelter. A grey cat named Pickle followed me around for two hours. I told myself I'm not allowed to adopt anything until I have a condo. Pickle did not accept this.

Tried a new recipe for bran muffins, a total disaster. I brought them to the staff room anyway and got three polite smiles. Dietitian pointed out that I used baking powder instead of soda. Lesson learned.
Mr. Alvarez came in for the Thursday sing-along but sat in the corner and said he would only play if the piano was fixed. He is seventy-four and very proud. I did not push. He did hum along, though.

Mortgage broker says I need another $18,000 for a decent down payment on even a one-bedroom. Currently at $41,000. Realistically a year and a half. Sometimes I wonder whether I should move to a cheaper city, but my residents are here.

Mr. Jin passed away on Saturday. He was one of my 'Moon River' men. I added a line to the binder and went and sat in the staff room for twenty minutes. Then I got up and ran bingo, because that is what he would have said to do.

Rain all day. I took my residents' favourite songs binder out and added two more. 'Moon River' now has four names against it. 'My Girl' has six. I think if I had to, I could run the whole programme just from that binder.
Long weekend, cooked too much butter chicken. Called mum. She wants me to come home for Thanksgiving but the wedding is that same month. Everything is happening in October.

messages.text:
Linda: Did you pick shoes yet?
Me: Not yet, I'm saving.
Linda: It's my wedding, I'll cover the shoes.
Me: That's very sweet, but you're already paying for too much.
Linda: Maya. Shoes.

Mr. Alvarez: I am sorry, Maya, I cannot play that piano. It hurts my ears and it embarrasses me.
Me: I understand. It hurts my ears too.
Mr. Alvarez: Find me a good one and I'll play every week.
Me: I'll try.

Karen: We cannot allocate money to the piano this year.
Me: Understood. Could we accept a donation if someone offered?
Karen: Of course, but it needs to be approved through the foundation first.
Me: Good to know.

Daughter: Thank you for writing down that she sang. It made my week.
Me: She did it all on her own. I just pressed play.
Daughter: Do you do this for everyone?
Me: Everyone I can.

Mum: Are you eating properly?
Me: Yes, I cooked a curry on Sunday.
Mum: You always say that. Send me a picture.
Me: Mum, it's a curry, it looks like curry.

Dev: Can you do a Saturday shift on the 17th?
Me: Yes, I've got it in the calendar.
Dev: Great. We got three new kittens in, one is orange.
Me: Dev, don't.

calendar.event: Shelter volunteer shift, 10 am to 2 pm
Train to Montreal for Linda's wedding (return Oct 26)

relations.about: Volunteer pianist, 74, retired high school music teacher. Won't play the home's out-of-tune piano. Very proud of his craft.
Administrator of the home. Supportive but constrained by budget.
Younger sister, getting married in Montreal in October.

constraints: Anything for the home must go through the foundation approval process
Residents get tired after 40 minutes, so sessions must be short
I work Monday to Friday, 8 to 4
No budget to pay for repairs from my own activity fund
No weekend work unless approved by admin
sensitive: Saving hard for a condo and feeling behind
Grief from residents passing away, harder than I tell people
Some tension with admin about the piano and the budget
Occasionally fantasizes about leaving care work because of burnout, but cannot imagine doing anything else
